 Right Arrow Robots Robot dogs mounted with rifles deployed in anti-gang stadium operation in Haiti
 Salvadoran special forces and Haitian police found human skulls inside Sylvio Cator Stadium during the joint operation
 By
 Brie Stimson Fox News 
 Published
 November 14, 2026 7:51pm EST Comments

 close Video El Salvador’s president shares video of gun-mounted robot dogs used in military operations 
 The video shared by El Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele suggested the robots assisted in an operation to take back a stadium from gang control in Haiti. (Credit: Presidency of El Salvador via AP)
 NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!
 El Salvador President Nayib Bukele released a video this week showing military forces using robotic dogs mounted with rifles in an operation to take back a stadium in Haiti from gang control.
 "Under the bilateral agreement between the Haitian government and the government of El Salvador , a joint operation involving the Haitian National Police, the Haitian Armed Forces (FAd’H), the Task Force, and the Salvadoran Special Forces successfully took control of Sylvio Cator Stadium and secured it," Bukele wrote on X in a translation from Haitian Creole.
 The video showed the robots moving down a hallway and up a set of stairs with the rifle on top.
 EL SALVADOR-BACKED AIR ASSAULT DESTROYS HAITI GANG HEADQUARTERS AMID SEARCH FOR MISSING TROOPS 
 El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele released footage Thursday showing military forces using robotic dogs mounted with rifles in an operation to take back a stadium in Haiti from gang control. (Nayib Bukele/X) 
 It’s unclear exactly how the robots assisted in the Port-au-Prince operation.
 Bukele said "several human skulls" were found inside the stadium during the operation.
 'THEY FED HIM HIS OWN EARS': TOP REPUBLICAN SHARES HORRIFYING STORIES OF GANG RULE IN HAITI 
 The video showed the robot climbing up a set of stairs. (Nayib Bukele/X) 
 "We will now establish an operational base at the stadium so we can continue advancing deeper into territory controlled by the gangs," he said. "We now have the upper hand on the ground."
 Bukele demanded gang members leave the area before their offensive began.
 JOHN KOUFOS: TRUMP’S ‘SHIELD OF THE AMERICAS’ COULD HELP DEFEND US FROM CARTELS 
 Bukele didn't elaborate on how the robots assisted in the stadium operation. (Nayib Bukele/X) 
 "Those who choose to stay and fight our forces will have to face the consequences," he said.
 CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP 
 Cracking down on gangs has been a hallmark of Bukele’s presidency since he took office in 2019.
 Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.
